intent_signal: Commercial-investigation / budget-planning. Searchers are pre-trip cost researchers deciding whether a multi-week-to-multi-month training stay in Thailand is financially feasible. The 'long-stay angle' query variants (train for a year, all-inclusive camp, DTV cost) reveal a sub-segment planning months/years — these users implicitly need a visa solution but the cost SERP and the DTV SERP are currently disconnected.
common_ground: All-in monthly budget benchmark of ~33,000-35,000 THB (~$1,000) for a disciplined non-Thai trainee; most quote $1,200-$2,000/mo realistic
Monthly unlimited training from ~10,000 THB (~$280) at smaller/Chiang Mai/Khao Lak gyms; 15,000 THB+ at comprehensive camps
Accommodation ~6,000-8,000 THB/mo basic near gym, up to 16,000-20,000 THB for bungalow/condo comfort
Food ~6,000-15,000 THB/mo depending on street-food vs Western
All-inclusive training+stay packages: ~$500-$1,500/mo (THB 30,000-100,000+; premium DTV bundles 80,000-150,000+ THB/mo)
Extended stays (1 month+) commonly earn 20-40% discounts
Phuket/Bangkok pricier than Chiang Mai / smaller towns
Fight income (local 3,000-4,000 THB, tourist 6,000-10,000 THB) noted by gym-authored pages

gap.description: Two SERPs that should be one are split. The cost SERP (Khao Lak, Tiger, ONE, Bangtao, hkt) quotes monthly prices but is visa-blind — none connect a long-stay budget to the DTV visa, the actual legal mechanism for training in Thailand for months or years. The DTV SERP is the mirror image: dominated by thin gym sales pages (punchit, petchnumnoi, fitfac, phuketmuaythai) selling 'acceptance-letter' course bundles with almost no honest total-cost-of-living modeling. Only topmuaythai.com bridges both (Chiang Mai costs + DTV), but it offers just three static budget scenarios — no interactive calculator, no breakdown of real recurring costs once you're ON the DTV (rent + training + food + the 500k THB bank requirement + per-entry realities over the 5-year term). Nobody offers: (1) an interactive monthly-budget estimator tied to the DTV long-stay reality, (2) honest Chiang Mai-specific long-stay figures contrasted with Phuket/Bangkok, (3) a clear 'what months/years of training actually costs and looks like' narrative that frames the DTV as the unlock rather than an afterthought.

weakness: Top organic results are either commercially biased gym rate cards or outdated editorial (ONE = 2019)
Zero featured snippet and no calculator/tool on any page — open lane for an interactive estimator to win rich engagement and possible snippet
DTV visa almost entirely absent from the cost SERP despite being the #1 long-stay enabler
No page credibly separates Chiang Mai long-stay economics from Phuket/Bangkok
DTV-cluster pages are thin sales letters with weak E-E-A-T and no genuine cost transparency
No page models the multi-month / multi-year reality (lifestyle inflation, recurring costs, what a year actually looks like)
recommended_angle: Position /dtv-visa/long-stay-training as the honest, Chiang-Mai-specific 'what months or years of training actually cost on a DTV visa' guide — anchored by an interactive monthly-budget estimator (training + rent + food + visa amortized over 5 years) that no competitor offers. It owns the long-stay/cost/DTV intersection the cost SERP ignores and the DTV sales pages fake, while deliberately deferring package/short-stay booking intent to the existing /stay-train pillar so the two never cannibalize.
